items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: an American named Sim Coppans, who had a jazz programme on radio for many years, were members of the Academy.

ctx.x: In December, I played in Geneva, Switzerland , and gave a few concerts with some nice Swiss musicians, Henri Chaix, a pianist of the style of James P. Johnson, and Willie 'the Lion' Smith; Pierre Bourru, a good drummer,and Michel Pilet, a sax tenor, with a nice sound in the style of Hawkins.

In February 1968, I was elected a member of the French Academy du Jazz. The function of the Academy du Jazz is to pick the best jazz records issued during the year and give it an award. There were distinctions for different categories, Blues, New Orleans, Modern Jazz, Singers, etc. We would also elect the best French musician of the year. A well known foreign musician who has been the European scene for years, the trumpetist Arthur Briggs, and an American named Sim Coppans, who had a jazz programme on radio for…

In May, Jeff Gilson asked me if I would accept to record an album of Negro Spirituals for a guy named Pou-Dubois who owned a studio. We recorded some well known spirituals and some which were completely unknown. Jeff made the arrangements. We made a contract stipulating that I would get royalties when Pou-Dubois would sell the tape and the record would be issued. We recorded the 8/9/11th of May, 1968. I had some nice French musicians with me such as Eddie Louis, Guy Peterson, etc.
